identification: Black painted kerosene (oil) side lamp with ribbed Fresnel lens, chimney top, brass filler cap, in the style of a Ford Model T era side lamp (c.1909-1916). Glossy black, clearly repainted. No maker name visible in the single photo; could be an original Model T style lamp (Brillie/Ford, Hellebore etc.) or a reproduction. Originals are usually found with brass trim and a maker stamp on the lens ring or door.

viewing_check: Look for a maker stamp or markings on lens ring, door, burner and bracket (Brillie, Ford script, Ford Script on lens, patent dates); check weight and metal (original is pressed steel with brass trim, repros are lighter and often have a sheen); check for the burner and font inside, bracket and mounting, lens cracks and rust under the paint. If marked Ford or an original maker, value is higher; if unmarked repro, it is a decor piece.
